messages.subject: Hierarchical negative binomial model
parts:
Hi,

I am new to Stan and am trying to construct a hierarchical model as per the following requirements:

response Y ~ neg_binomial_2( mu.y , phi.y )  ## the dots are only for explanation purposes here; the parameters are not named with dots in the Stan code.

where, mu.y = exp(a) * X^b  ## This is a biologically meaningful and established relationship for the variables being measured in this system.

and, X is itself drawn from a negative binomial distribution    X ~ neg_binomial_2( lamda , phi.x) with lamda ~ lognormal( lamda.bar , sigma)

lamda.bar = mean(X.obs.plot), where X.obs is a vector of the observed values of the predictor at that location/plot, measured over multiple years. The expected number of X for a plot is lamda and these were drawn from a lognormal distribution with mean lamda.bar and variance sigma sq.

FYI, to give you an idea of why I need to undertake this joint modeling of the probability distribution of Y: 

In this data, the response Y was measured in plots adjacent to where the predictor X.obs was measured. This spatial mismatch implies that the values of Y do not correspond to the true value of X at that location, but have to be estimated from X.obs. Additionally, in many cases, the value of X.obs is 0 but there is a non-zero value for Y. This again occurs due to the spatial mismatch mentioned above. Therefore, the actual values of X used to obtain mu.y for the negative binomial distribution for estimating the response Y, have to be drawn from the values of X.obs. The response Y has to modeled from a joint probability distribution of the expected values for X and Y.

I've pasted my code and error messages below. There might be something very basic in the coding that I am unable to understand and hence going wrong with. Any help will be much appreciated! 

Thank you for your time.

Best,
Meghna

perspp.nb.hier<-"
data{
  int<lower=0> N; //no.of data points
  vector[N] seed; //predictor: positive real number, range= 0 - 50000 (~60% values are zeros)
  int<lower=0> sdl[N]; //response: integer, range = 0 - 212 (~50% values are zeros)
}

parameters{
  real sigma;
  real<lower=0> lamda;
  real<lower=0> phisd;
  real alpha;
  real beta;
  real<lower=0> phisdl;
}

model{
  int seed2[N];
  sigma ~ uniform(0,10);
  phisd ~ uniform(0,10);
  alpha ~ uniform(0,100);
  beta ~ uniform(0,10);
  phisdl ~ uniform(0,10);
  for(i in 1:N){
    lamda[i] ~ lognormal(seed[i], sigma);
    seed2[i] ~ neg_binomial_2(lamda[i], phisd);
    }
    sdl ~ neg_binomial_2_log(exp(alpha)*seed2^beta, phisdl);
  }
}"

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Hierarchical negative binomial model
parts:
May I ask what you read before you tried to write this
model? The reason I ask is that the two problems in your
code are quite common and we'd like to be able to more
clearly formulate the issues.

Issue 1.

The variables in Stan need to be declared with constraints
so that any value satisfying the constraints has finite
log density. So when you have a parameter declared
as

> real sigma;

and a sampling statement

> sigma ~ uniform(0,10);

you produce a problem where sigma < 0 or sigma > 10 satsify
the declared constraints (there aren't any).

If you insist on this prior, you need to declare

real<lower=0, upper=10> sigma;

and similarly for the other parameters.

Issue 2.

You are using the local variable seed2 before it is defined:

int seed2[N];
...

Stan doesn't work like BUGS --- this just increments the posterior
log density. In BUGS, it defines an edge in a directed graphical
model.

I think the only solution is to marginalize seed2 out of your
model. I'm not sure how a compound negative binomial works. You're
giving your model a double-dose of overdispersion.

Issue 3.

You can't raise an array to a power, so seed2^beta is going to
be ill-formed as well. The legal signatures are defined in the
index to the manual.

- Bob

​1. Can I define seed2 as a vector instead and use the ​generated quantities option to determine the values of seed2 from the distribution that describes it? I couldn't determine a way to draw random values from a prescribed distribution in Stan, as can be done in R.

May I ask what you read before you tried to write this
model?  The reason I ask is that the two problems in your
code are quite common and we'd like to be able to more
clearly formulate the issues.

Issue 1.

The variables in Stan need to be declared with constraints
so that any value satisfying the constraints has finite
log density.  So when you have a parameter declared
as

>   real sigma;

and a sampling statement

>   sigma ~ uniform(0,10);

you produce a problem where sigma < 0 or sigma > 10 satsify
the declared constraints (there aren't any).

If you insist on this prior, you need to declare

  real<lower=0, upper=10> sigma;

and similarly for the other parameters.

Issue 2.

You are using the local variable seed2 before it is defined:

  int seed2[N];
  ...
    seed2[i] ~ neg_binomial_2(lamda[i], phisd);

Stan doesn't work like BUGS --- this just increments the posterior
log density.  In BUGS, it defines an edge in a directed graphical
model.

I think the only solution is to marginalize seed2 out of your
model.  I'm not sure how a compound negative binomial works.  You're
giving your model a double-dose of overdispersion.

Issue 3.

You can't raise an array to a power, so seed2^beta is going to
be ill-formed as well.  The legal signatures are defined in the
index to the manual.

- Bob

we have the entire model to look at. You can probably vectorize
that code to be much more efficient if lambda, seed2, and sdl are
1D containers (vectors or 1D arrays).

In this case, for Stan, seed2 and sdl would need to be data.
Stan can't sample discrete parameters.

- Bob
